title: Critical Properties and Glass Transitions in Randomly Coupled Fields
abstract: We study an assembly of $N$ scalar fields coupled via a quenched random interaction, equivalent to a spin glass whose spins are promoted to $d$-dimensional fields. When $N$ is large, the random coupling matrix produces a family of Gaussian universality classes whose critical exponents are determined by the behavior of the eigenvalue density near the spectral edge. For a Wigner matrix, the correlation length diverges at criticality but the susceptibility remains finite, and one-loop replica analysis supports an upper critical dimension of unity. In an exactly solvable spherical variant, the heat capacity jumps at the transition in $d>1$, and correlations remain pinned to their critical form throughout the glass phase, giving generic scale invariance despite the absence of a Goldstone mode.
summary: This work investigates the critical phenomena in systems of randomly coupled, extended scalar fields, treating the system as a generalization of a spin glass. Using replica theory and large-N limits, the authors derive scaling laws and determine the upper critical dimension for the transition. The results provide deep insights into how disorder governs phase transitions in extended quantum or classical field theories.
main_problem: The paper characterizes the critical behavior and universality classes of systems composed of a large number of spatially extended, randomly coupled scalar fields.
main_result: The analysis determines an upper critical dimension ($d_u$) for the system, finding $d_u=1$ for the Wigner case, and shows that the heat capacity exhibits a discontinuity at the critical point for $d>1$.
method: The study employs the replica formalism combined with the saddle point method to evaluate the quenched-averaged free energy and analyze the stability of the replica-symmetric solution.
model_or_system: The model consists of $N$ scalar fields coupled by a quenched random interaction, analogous to a spin glass where spins are promoted to fields. A specific, exactly solvable variant is the Spherical Model.

paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the general Gaussian theory, then analyzing the nonlinear case using the replica formalism, and finally examining the stability of the saddle point solution via the Hessian matrix.
why_interesting: The techniques used—replica methods and analyzing critical exponents in random media—are foundational to understanding complex many-body systems, which share mathematical parallels with quantum many-body physics.
